suite: Transformations on TPC-H, TPC-DS and JOB
score: 233/235 changed queries return the same rows on the real data, 0 wrong (231 proven)
metric: KumoSQL's cleanup pipeline (rules, then formatter) applied to the official TPC-H (21), TPC-DS (102) and JOB (113) queries; every changed query is run against the original in DuckDB on the benchmark's own data (TPC-H SF0.1, TPC-DS SF1, IMDB) and on generated tables.
correctness: 0 proven rewrites returned different rows: 233 changed queries agree on real data, 1 more only on generated tables (its original does not run in DuckDB on real data), 1 not runnable anywhere. Every rule run on its own as well: 0 wrong.
held_out: 38/39 same on real data, 0 wrong (hash-held-out fifth; no implementation changes were made in this work, only harness fixes)
command: python tools/benchmark_corpora.py fetch sqlstorm tpch-data tpcds-data job-data && python tools/transformation_bench.py tpch tpcds job
caveats: Original queries only (one instance per template from SQLStorm v0.0 and gregrahn/join-order-benchmark); TPC-H query 13 is left out because sqlglot cannot convert it. The same TPC queries also appear in the Analytical SQL coverage sample. proven = rewritten and same when executed; unknown = unchanged; unsupported = not runnable. DuckDB is the oracle, not BigQuery. Formatting changes almost every query, so the structural-rule counts are under usefulness.
usefulness: Structural rules made 80 changes (subquery lifting 45, parentheses 18, CTE inlining 17); DuckDB planned 21 of them differently and 4 ran at least 5% faster. Pipeline median speed-up 1.01: DuckDB already unnests subqueries and inlines CTEs.
performance: Pipeline per query: median 1.1 s TPC-H, 2.2 s TPC-DS (max 26 s), 1.2 s JOB; each structural rule 7 to 29 ms median, the rest is the sqlfluff formatter
